title.rendered: Calling Things That Are Not as Though They Were | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 4

excerpt.rendered: Abraham’s God is the God who calls what does not exist as though it already did. Day 4 teaches the Romans 4:17 habit, speaking from the finish line, not the start.

content.rendered:
God named Abraham “father of many nations” while he was still childless. Faith learns to speak from the finish line while the race is still being run.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, October 21, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 4

Today’s Scripture

“(As it is written, ‘I have made you a father of many nations’) in the presence of Him whom he believed, God, who gives life to the dead and calls those things which do not exist as though they did.”
Romans 4:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Abraham’s story is the DNA of New Testament faith. Before he had one child, God renamed him Abraham, “father of a multitude.” Every time he introduced himself for the next quarter of a century, he was prophesying. The NKJV captures the heart of it in Romans 4:17: God “calls those things which do not exist as though they did.” The AMPC deepens it: God “speaks of the nonexistent things that [He has foretold and promised] as if they [already] existed.” The TPT renders it: God “calls into being things that don’t even exist yet.”

This is not denial. Abraham did not pretend he already had a son. Verse 19 says plainly, “Not being weak in faith, he did not consider his own body, already dead.” He saw the facts; he just refused to let the facts have the last word. He called things that were not as though they were, because the God who had promised was not a God of possibilities; He was a God of accomplished facts not yet delivered to time.

In Lagos a trader is naming a business that is still a sketch. In London a student is already answering to a title God gave her in prayer. In Manila a church is confessing a building that is still a plot of weeds. In Nairobi and São Paulo, mothers are addressing children not yet born as if their callings were already settled. This is not fantasy. This is Abrahamic faith operating by Romans 4:17, vocamus ea quae non sunt tanquam sint, as the Latin fathers rendered it: “we call the things that are not as though they are.”

Jesus walked in this habit perfectly. He called Simon “Peter” (rock) before Simon was anything close to a rock (John 1:42). He called Matthew from a tax table and spoke apostleship over him. He told His disciples, “You are the light of the world,” while they were still arguing about who was greatest. God names you from the finish line. Faith learns to answer to that name while the race is still being run.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Find what God has already called you in His Word, healed, redeemed, forgiven, royal, chosen, more than a conqueror. These are not aspirations. These are facts in Christ.

Personalise. Call yourself by what God calls you. Abraham lived twenty-five years under a prophetic name before he saw it fulfilled. Live under yours.

Proclaim. Speak in the perfect tense when the Word speaks in the perfect tense. “By His stripes I am healed,” not “will be.” “I am seated with Christ,” not “hope to be.”

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I serve the God who calls the things that are not as though they are. I belong to Abraham’s household by faith, so I inherit Abraham’s habit. I will not consider only what is visible. I speak from the finish line, not the start. I am healed, I am supplied, I am seated with Christ in heavenly places. My seed is blessed; my work is blessed; my coming in and my going out are blessed. What God has called me, I answer to. What God has promised me, I confess. The nonexistent, at His word, is more real than the visible, at the devil’s suggestion. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
